# What is Vault Client?

Vault Client is a client-only edition of Vault Enterprise for applications and
systems that consume secrets from Vault. Vault Client includes Vault Agent,
Vault Proxy, and a subset of the Vault CLI. It does not include the Vault
server.

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

You need a Vault Enterprise license to download Vault Client, but Vault Client
does not need a license key to run.

<Note title="Vault Client is different from Vault clients">

  Vault Client is the name of a Vault Enterprise binary and container image.
  Vault also uses the word [client](/vault/docs/concepts/billing/clients) for
  anything that connects and authenticates to Vault, such as a user or an
  application.

</Note>

## Why use Vault Client?

Use Vault Client on systems that authenticate to Vault and consume secrets, but
do not run a Vault server:

- **Deploy a smaller binary.** The `vault-client` binary is about one tenth the
  size of the full `vault` binary.

- **Reduce your attack surface.** Vault Client leaves out the Vault server and
  has about half as many dependencies as the full `vault` binary, so there is
  less code to scan and patch on client systems.

- **Upgrade clients on their own schedule.** You can upgrade Vault Client more
  often than your Vault servers. Refer to
  [Server compatibility](#server-compatibility) for details.

## What Vault Client includes

Vault Client includes the following components:

- **[Vault Agent](/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent)**. Start Vault Agent with
  `vault-client agent`.
- **[Vault Proxy](/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/proxy)**. Start Vault Proxy with
  `vault-client proxy`.
- **A subset of [Vault CLI commands](#cli-commands)**.
-  **[TPM authentication](/vault/docs/auth/tpm/tpm#configure-the-tpm-auth-method)**.

Vault Agent and Vault Proxy in Vault Client support the same features as the
full `vault` binary and use the same configuration files. To move an existing
Vault Agent or Vault Proxy deployment to Vault Client, replace `vault` with
`vault-client` in the command that starts it. For example:

```shell-session
$ vault-client agent -config=/etc/vault/agent.hcl
```

### CLI commands ((#cli-commands))

Included commands behave the same as they do in the full `vault` binary. The
following table lists each Vault CLI command and whether Vault Client includes
it:

| Command | Vault Client |
| --- | --- |
| [`agent`](/vault/docs/commands/agent) | Included |
| `audit` | Not included |
| [`auth`](/vault/docs/commands/auth) | Included |
| [`debug`](/vault/docs/commands/debug) | Not included |
| [`delete`](/vault/docs/commands/delete) | Included |
| [`events`](/vault/docs/commands/events) | Not included |
| `hcp` | Included |
| [`kv`](/vault/docs/commands/kv) | Included |
| [`lease`](/vault/docs/commands/lease) | Included |
| [`license`](/vault/docs/commands/license) | Not included |
| [`list`](/vault/docs/commands/list) | Included |
| [`login`](/vault/docs/commands/login) | Included |
| [`monitor`](/vault/docs/commands/monitor) | Not included |
| [`namespace`](/vault/docs/commands/namespace) | Included |
| [`operator`](/vault/docs/commands/operator) | Only `key-status`, `rotate`, and `unseal` |
| [`patch`](/vault/docs/commands/patch) | Included |
| [`path-help`](/vault/docs/commands/path-help) | Included |
| [`pki`](/vault/docs/commands/pki) | Not included |
| [`plugin`](/vault/docs/commands/plugin) | Not included |
| [`policy`](/vault/docs/commands/policy) | Not included |
| [`print`](/vault/docs/commands/print) | Included |
| [`proxy`](/vault/docs/commands/proxy) | Included |
| [`read`](/vault/docs/commands/read) | Included |
| [`recover`](/vault/docs/commands/recover) | Included |
| [`secrets`](/vault/docs/commands/secrets) | Included |
| [`server`](/vault/docs/commands/server) | Not included |
| [`ssh`](/vault/docs/commands/ssh) | Included |
| [`status`](/vault/docs/commands/status) | Included |
| [`token`](/vault/docs/commands/token) | Included |
| `tpm`, refer to the [TPM auth method](/vault/docs/auth/tpm/tpm#configure-the-tpm-auth-method) | Included |
| [`transform`](/vault/docs/commands/transform) | Not included |
| [`transit`](/vault/docs/commands/transit) | Not included |
| [`unwrap`](/vault/docs/commands/unwrap) | Included |
| [`version`](/vault/docs/commands/version) | Included |
| [`version-history`](/vault/docs/commands/version-history) | Not included |
| [`write`](/vault/docs/commands/write) | Included |

When you run a command that Vault Client does not include, `vault-client`
prints an error that names the command and links to the full Vault binary, and
exits with status code `1`. Vault Client also hides those commands from help
output and autocomplete. Use the full `vault` binary to run them.

You can call any Vault API endpoint with the `read`, `write`, `list`, `delete`,
and `patch` commands. For example, Vault Client does not include the `transit`
command, but you can encrypt data with the Transit secrets engine by writing to
its API path:

```shell-session
$ vault-client write transit/encrypt/my-key plaintext=$(base64 <<< "my secret data")
```

Refer to [Calling API endpoints](/vault/docs/commands#calling-api-endpoints)
for more information.

## Server compatibility ((#server-compatibility))

Vault Client 2.x works with Vault Enterprise 2.x servers and HCP Vault
Dedicated. We recommend running the same major and minor version of Vault
Client as your Vault servers, but you can upgrade Vault Client more often than
your servers.

## Platforms

Vault Client is available for the following platforms. All Vault Client
artifacts are Tier 1, and we test them in IPv6 mode. Refer to
[OS validation](/vault/docs/partners/protocols#os-validation) for test
environments.

| Operating system | Architectures | Binary | Container image |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x | Yes | Yes |
| AIX | ppc64 | Yes | No |
| Windows | 386, amd64 | Yes | No |

## Get Vault Client

Vault Client is available only from IBM Passport Advantage Online and the IBM
Entitled Registry:

- **IBM Passport Advantage Online** provides Vault Client binaries and
  container image archives.
- **IBM Entitled Registry** (`cp.icr.io`) provides Vault Client container
  images.

Vault Client is not available from the HashiCorp releases site, Docker Hub,
Amazon ECR, the Red Hat Ecosystem Catalog, or package managers. Refer to
[Install Vault Client](/vault/docs/client/install) for instructions.
